description: Expected differences between CDK and Terraform deployments for the minimal fixture. These are documented, intentional divergences arising from architectural decisions in the Terraform translation layer.

allowedMissingInTerraform.reason: Terraform modules encapsulate IAM policies inside module bodies rather than emitting discrete aws_iam_policy resources. The IAM permissions are still created but are not visible as top-level plan resources.
API Gateway Lambda permissions in Terraform are handled via the aws_lambda_permission resource inside the api module. The current tf-modules/api module may not yet emit these; tracked in HOM-21.
The Terraform api module uses a proxy integration which may not emit a discrete aws_apigateway_resource for the proxy path.
Method resources may be folded into the aws_api_gateway_integration inside the Terraform api module.
Terraform aws_api_gateway_rest_api handles deployment implicitly or via a separate deployment resource that may use a different naming pattern.
Stage may be managed implicitly by the Terraform api module rather than as a discrete resource.
The Terraform storage-drive module may inline the bucket policy inside the aws_s3_bucket resource rather than emitting a separate aws_s3_bucket_policy.
Queue policy may be inlined inside the aws_sqs_queue resource in the Terraform queue module.

Lambda warming is controlled by the disableLambdaWarming flag in the fixture. CDK still emits the warmer rule because the construct is unconditional in BootstrapQpqServiceStack; Terraform may omit it when disabled.
Same as above — Terraform bootstrap module may skip SNS warmer topic when lambda warming is disabled.
Same as above — Terraform bootstrap module may skip SNS warmer topic policy when lambda warming is disabled.

CDK uses a custom resource provider for S3 auto-delete. Terraform storage-drive module handles bucket cleanup via lifecycle rules or force_destroy, eliminating the need for the custom resource and its IAM role.
Same as above — Terraform does not need the S3 auto-delete custom resource Lambda function.
Terraform queue module may inline the IAM policy for the queue Lambda inside the module rather than emitting a discrete policy resource.

allowedMissingInCdk.reason: Terraform storage-drive module may emit a separate aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource for compliance, while CDK inlines this inside the bucket properties.

allowedPropertyDiffs.reason: CDK uses apiGatewayEventHandler as the handler name; Terraform service-function module may use a different entry-point wrapper.
CDK uses anyExecuteServiceFunctionEvent_serviceFunction as the handler name; Terraform module may use a different wrapper.
CDK uses sqsEvent_queueEvent as the handler name; Terraform module may use a different wrapper.
CDK logical ID hash suffix vs Terraform module naming may differ slightly in the suffix format, but both follow the QPQ naming convention.
Same as above — naming suffix format may differ between CDK and Terraform while both follow QPQ convention.
